title: The augmented simplicial ph-etale comparison square
statement:
Let $a:U_\bullet\to X$ be a simplicial scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object] with an augmentation (a natural map to the constant scheme $X$). Use small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], big ph sites [def-trf-ph-scheme-site], geometric morphisms [def-trf-geometric-morphism], and the common size convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $h_T:\mathrm{Sh}((\mathrm{Sch}/T)_{ph})\to\mathrm{Sh}(T_{\mathrm{Et}})$ be induced by the inclusion of etale $T$-schemes into all $T$-schemes. There is a geometric morphism $h:\mathrm{Sh}((\mathrm{Sch}/U_\bullet)_{ph,total})\to\mathrm{Sh}(U_{\bullet,\mathrm{Et}})$ with components $h_{U_n}$. Precisely, for each $n$ the inclusion functor $V\mapsto V/U_n$ from etale $U_n$-schemes to all $U_n$-schemes is the continuous functor defining the morphism of sites underlying $h_{U_n}$; these morphisms commute with the simplicial structure morphisms of the two families of sites through the canonical identifications of iterated fibre products, and $h$ is the morphism of total topoi they induce, so that $(h^{-1}G)_n=h_{U_n}^{-1}G_n$ and $(h_*F)_n=h_{U_n,*}F_n$. The two total topoi have sheaves given by families on their component sites with transition maps $u_\alpha^{-1}F_p\to F_q$ satisfying the identity and composition rules [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. If $b$ denotes the ph augmentation and $a$ the etale augmentation, the square commutes by a canonical isomorphism
$$a\circ h\simeq h_X\circ b,\qquad h^{-1}a^{-1}\simeq b^{-1}h_X^{-1}.$$
The inverse-image isomorphism in component $n$ is the canonical comparison $h_{U_n}^{-1}a_n^{-1}\simeq b_n^{-1}h_X^{-1}$ induced by the same etale-object inclusion. No properness, surjectivity or hypercover hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tag 0DHJ, lemma-compare-simplicial-objects-ph-etale, using the scheme version explicitly permitted in section-proper-hypercovering-spaces; Tag 0D99, lemma-morphism-augmentation-simplicial-sites.

proof.text: Use $\mathcal C=(\mathrm{Sch}/X)_{ph}$ and regard the augmentation as a simplicial object over the terminal object $X/X$. This category has all fibre products. The slice-site theorem supplies its simplicial diagram of sites, total site, and augmentation $b$. The slice at $U_n/X$ is $(\mathrm{Sch}/U_n)_{ph}$: an object is exactly a scheme over $U_n$, and its covering families are generated by the Zariski families of open immersions whose images cover the target and by singleton proper-surjective maps, exactly as in the current ph-site definition. For a structure map $u_\alpha:U_q\to U_p$, the continuous functor is $W\mapsto W\times_{U_p}U_q$. On the small etale sites the same base-change rule defines a morphism of sites by the set-valued etale inverse-image theorem. Thus the two families are simplicial diagrams of sites. In both diagrams the composition isomorphism $(W\times_{U_p}U_q)\times_{U_q}U_r\cong W\times_{U_p}U_r$ preserves the projections to $W$ and $U_r$. Two composites of these isomorphisms agree because maps to a fibre product are determined by those projections. This verifies the required coherence, including identities.

source.place: Tag 0DHJ proof, case A and Tag 09WL; small etale functoriality as in section-simplicial-algebraic-spaces.

proof.text: For every scheme $T$ take the geometric morphism $h_T$ induced by the etale-object inclusion, whose existence is explicitly part of the ph/etale comparison statement. Only that first assertion is used, so no complex or torsion assumption enters. Write $i_T(V)=V/T$. For any scheme morphism $f:T'\to T$ and any etale $V\to T$, the two composites of site functors, inclusion followed by big base change and small base change followed by inclusion, both give $(V\times_TT')/T'$. The same holds on arrows: both send $g$ to $g\times_T\mathrm{id}_{T'}$. Hence their canonical identification commutes with all arrows. The composition theorem for morphisms of sites turns this into the comparison of geometric morphisms $f_{\mathrm{Et}}h_{T'}\simeq h_T f_{ph}$. It also identifies the comparison of inverse images with that of these very site functors. For composites of $f$ the comparisons agree: their underlying fibre-product maps preserve the same projections, and the adjunction-compatible composition identifications are unique. Here $f_{ph}$ is the morphism of sites given by big base change, supplied by the slice-site theorem for the simplicial operators and for the augmentation maps $a_n$, the only maps to which this is applied. Apply this first to all simplicial operators.

source.place: Tag 0DHJ proof, functors $U_{n,etale}	o(\mathrm{Sch}/U_n)_{ph}$; scheme comparison in etale-cohomology.tex section-ph-etale, Tag 0DDX (lemma-push-pull-ph-etale).

proof.text: The total-site theorem now applies to the two diagrams and the coherent component morphisms of steps 1--2. It supplies $h$ and the description of total sheaves as families with inverse-image transition maps. Here the underlying functor on total sites applies $i_{U_n}$ in degree $n$. It is continuous because coverings lie in a single degree and each $i_{U_n}$ is continuous; pullbacks of such coverings are respected by step 2. By the continuous-functor sheaf adjunction its direct image is precomposition. Evaluating on an etale $V/U_n$ gives $(h_*F)_n(V)=F_n(i_{U_n}V)=(h_{U_n,*}F_n)(V)$, including the restriction maps. The left adjoint on families sends $G_n$ to $h_{U_n}^{-1}G_n$; its transitions use the comparison from step 2 and then the transition of $G$. Indeed, a componentwise adjoint pair of maps $h_{U_n}^{-1}G_n\to F_n$ and $G_n\to h_{U_n,*}F_n$ satisfies the transition squares on one side if and only if it does on the other, by naturality of the component adjunctions. This is an adjunction on families, so its left adjoint is $h^{-1}$. This proves the two component formulas for sheaves of sets, as well as for abelian sheaves.

source.place: Tag 0DHJ proof and Tag 0D96, lemma-morphism-simplicial-sites, case A, explicit componentwise adjunction.

proof.text: Apply the calculation of step 2 to each augmentation map $a_n:U_n\to X$. For every etale $V/X$, both site-functor composites give $(V\times_XU_n)/U_n$, where $b_n$ is the base-change morphism of sites, which by the slice-site theorem has the same geometric morphism as the localization morphism; so the composition theorem gives the specified natural inverse-image isomorphism $\theta_n:h_{U_n}^{-1}a_n^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}b_n^{-1}h_X^{-1}$. For a simplicial operator $u_\alpha:U_q\to U_p$, the transition compatibility of $\theta_p$ and $\theta_q$ is the identification $(V\times_XU_p)\times_{U_p}U_q\cong V\times_XU_q$. The two maps to the latter fibre product have the same projections to $V$ and $U_q$; hence they are equal. This verifies compatibility with both faces and degeneracies, not merely the equality of the component objects.

In the family description the inverse image of the etale augmentation is $G\mapsto(a_n^{-1}G)_n$, with the canonical composition transition isomorphisms; this is the defining augmentation construction. The ph augmentation has the corresponding description by the slice-site theorem. Step 3 therefore identifies the components of $h^{-1}a^{-1}G$ with $h_{U_n}^{-1}a_n^{-1}G$, and those of $b^{-1}h_X^{-1}G$ with $b_n^{-1}h_X^{-1}G$. The compatible isomorphisms $\theta_n$ of step 4 and their inverses define inverse natural morphisms of these families. Thus $h^{-1}a^{-1}\simeq b^{-1}h_X^{-1}$ with the required component normalization. Taking the corresponding isomorphism of geometric morphisms gives $a\circ h\simeq h_X\circ b$. The construction used arbitrary scheme morphisms and an augmentation only; it does not use properness, surjectivity, or a hypercover condition.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q116-4353d7f78 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read in full: the item, the new node lem-trf-slice-site-simplicial-augmentation, the statements of all 14 cited nodes, and the parent's uses of the item. Stacks sources read: spaces-simplicial.tex 0DHJ with its proof, the preamble of section-proper-hypercovering-spaces (which allows schemes), 09WL with its proof, 0D70, 0D96 case A, 0D99 and its remark, and sites.tex 09W9. The item's statement agrees with 0DHJ: it assumes only an augmentation and adds no hypothesis, and its component and normalization clauses are what 0D96 and 0D99 prove. Its statement is unchanged and not weakened. Coefficients are sheaves of sets and abelian sheaves follow; there is no six-functor base-change morphism here. Steps 1, 3 and 5 are correct. In step 1 I checked by hand that the localized ph topology equals the ph topology of Sch/U_n, because the generators are stable under base change. The new node is a site-general form of 09WL plus 0D70, not a clause of the item. It has the needed small-site and fibre-product hypotheses. I tested it on a one-object terminal site, a constant simplicial object with the identity augmentation, and empty schemes. No duplicate exists: grep for 09WL, 0DHJ, 09W9 and sr-when-fibre-products found nothing, and total-site-derived-components, site-augmentation-acyclic-cech and site-hypercover-derived-descent state other things. One fault, fixed (C1/C3): step 4 builds theta_n with the composition theorem applied to the base-change site functors V/X -> (V x_X U_n)/U_n. This needs each b_n to be the base-change morphism of sites, but the new node only called b_n the localization morphism, the identification (Sites 09W9, cited in the 09WL proof) is in no DAG node, and step 4 did not cite the new node. Step 2 likewise needs f_ph as a morphism of sites without citing where it comes from. Fix: one sentence added to the new node's statement, saying each b_n is the morphism of sites given by W -> W x_X U_n with the same geometric morphism and (b_{n,*}F)(W)=F(W x_X U_n), with 09W9 added to its source. Steps 2 and 4 now cite the new node, with one sentence each. proof_deps and the item statement are unchanged. lean.statement: theorem simplicial_ph_etale_square {U : SimplicialObject Scheme.{u}} {X : Scheme.{u}} (a : U ⟶ (Functor.const SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ).obj X) : (∀ n : ℕ, IsIso (inverseComponentMap a n)) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, IsIso (ordinaryAugmentationComponentMap a n)) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, IsIso (ordinaryComponentSquareMap (a.app (op (SimplexCategory.mk n))))) ∧ IsIso (squareMap a) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, whiskerRight (ordinaryAugmentationComponentMap a n) (componentComparison (a.app (op (SimplexCategory.mk n)))).inverse ≫ whiskerLeft (etaleAugmentation a).inverse (inverseComponentMap a n) ≫ whiskerRight (squareMap a) (phRestriction a n) ≫ whiskerLeft (Scheme.phEtaleGeometricMorphism.{u, u} X).inverse (phAugmentationComponentIso a n).hom = ordinaryComponentSquareMap (a.app (op (SimplexCategory.mk n))))
